why: Most-used name wins (Ana, 2026-08-17). This is sold and searched for as simply 'climbing hydrangea'; the 'Japanese' qualifier is a variant nobody types. The name became free the same day, when the duplicate row Hydrangea anomala that held it was removed - and that row holding the better name is part of why the pair read as duplicates. The scientific name is left as Hydrangea petiolaris under the same rule: the accepted botanical name is H. anomala subsp. petiolaris, but every nursery label and plant list shortens it to this.

Ana, 2026-08-17, overruling round 13's step 1a. curate-common-names chose 'Hardy chrysanthemum' to distinguish this from Chrysanthemum indicum, which the catalog holds as 'Indian chrysanthemum'. The distinguishing was right and the name was not: florist's chrysanthemum is the standard English name for the garden hybrid, and it separates the two just as well. It also matches a construction the catalog already uses for exactly this kind of cultivated-hybrid-versus-species pair, in 'Florist's cyclamen'. Applied before curate-editorial reached the row, since a signed-off row is frozen against a mechanical name write.
